taskloom Configuration.

These fields map to `~/.taskloom/config.yaml` (and the per-project `.taskloom/config.yaml`). The canonical machine-readable form is the JSON Schema at `resources/schema/input/taskloom-config-schema.json`.

## Overriding From The Environment Or A CLI Flag

Every field on this page can also be set without editing a config file, in ascending precedence: the home config file, then the project config file, then an environment variable, then a `--config-set` flag — the last one that sets a given key wins.

An environment variable override starts with `TASKLOOM_CONFIG_`, followed by the field's dotted path with each segment upper-cased and joined by `_` (e.g. `agents.mycoder.runtime` becomes `TASKLOOM_CONFIG_AGENTS_MYCODER_RUNTIME`). A CLI override uses the repeatable `--config-set <dotted.path>=<value>` flag (`--config-set agents.mycoder.runtime=container`) — never a per-field flag of its own, since a command's OWN flags (`--format`, `--bundle`, ...) are not config overrides. Both forms are matched case-insensitively against whatever your config file already has, adopting its casing; unlike an environment variable's name, `--config-set`'s path preserves whatever case you type, so it can also CREATE a new case-sensitive key (e.g. `--config-set agents.MyCoder.runtime=container`), which an environment variable cannot do.

For example, `homing` can be set via `TASKLOOM_CONFIG_HOMING=<value>` or `--config-set homing=<value>`.

## Top-Level Fields

Schema for taskloom's own config.yaml files (~/.taskloom/config.yaml and the per-project .taskloom/config.yaml), layered via internal/shared/confload exactly like ctxloom's own config-schema.json.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `homing` | string | Where the project's task-store log is homed. "home" keeps it PRIVATE under ~/.ctxloom/tasks/<project-id>.jsonl (today's default behavior; never committed, never shared by a clone). "repo" checks the log into the project tree at .taskloom/tasks.jsonl, alongside this config file, so it is SHAREABLE and travels with clones. taskloom refuses to guess: this key (at either the home or project config layer), the TASKLOOM_CONFIG_HOMING environment variable, or the --homing flag must set it before any command that touches a single project's store will run. Allowed values: `home`, `repo`. |
| `tag_schema` | string[] | Tag-schema declarations, each written in tagma's own tag syntax, asserting a facet over a tag key used on this project's tasks — e.g. `tagma.arity:"triage:type"=scalar`. Today only the `arity` facet is enforced: a target declared `=scalar` may carry at most one tag with that (namespace, key) per task, and taskloom's write seam collapses a re-tag onto it (the newest value survives; the log still records both the retracting untag and the new tag, so history is never rewritten) — see internal/shared/tasks/tagschema and internal/shared/tasks/operations. `tagma.priority_fn:"<key>"="<mustache-equation>"` and `tagma.decay_fn:"<key>"="<mustache-equation>"` declarations are parsed and stored but not yet evaluated (a later ranking feature). This key replaces the WHOLE list at whichever layer sets it last (home < project < TASKLOOM_CONFIG_* env < --config-set) — it is never merged element-by-element. Unset at every layer falls back to taskloom's built-in triage-classification baseline: `triage:type` and `triage:impact` declared scalar, plus that baseline's own priority_fn/decay_fn declarations for `triage:impact`. |
